note: A senior IT professional in AI product development, working on large deals and managing systems whose failures pull him away at any hour — 'successful' on the 'or equivalent' reading, though he is an employee rather than a business owner or physician. 'Neglected health' fits well: movement was the one constant in his life until the last eighteen to twenty-four months of added responsibility. 'Good to great' is explicit and unusually clear — he does five to ten pull-ups, trains twice daily with a kettlebell, and frames the goal as 'I don't think I've ever unlocked my real potential' rather than rescue. Plainly 'not deconditioned'. He fails 'income' outright and by his own words: sole breadwinner for a family of four, expected price point $250/month against $1,000, and 'at this higher pricing, I don't know if I can afford it, to be very honest with you.' This is the same shape as the Badrane Hriouch assessment — fits on profile, fails on willingness or capacity to pay — but with an important difference: there the rep recognised it and disqualified rather than discounted, whereas here the rep ran a downsell and then suggested selling household possessions. Also relevant to the corpus observation that income screening may filter out deals the payment plan could carry: the plan was offered, priced live in two configurations, and did not carry it.
